The chariots of Rāhu and Ketu are fitted with eight horses each. All these planets are bound to Dhruva (Pole Star) by reins which are of the form of wind. Made to whirl by the Pole star they move ahead.

## \|\| 57.6 \|\|

*yāvantyaścaiva tārāś ca tāvantaścaiva raśmayaḥ \|*  
*sarve dhruvanibaddhāś ca bhramanto bhrāmayanti tam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. There are as many rays as there are stars. All of them are bound to the Pole star. While revolving (round it) they make it revolve also.

## \|\| 57.7 \|\|

*alātacakravadyānti vātacakreritāni tu \|*  
*yasmādvahati jyotīṃṣi pravahastena sa smṛtaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The stars and the luminaries, urged by the circular gusts of wind, move like fire brands. Since the wind bears the luminaries, it is called Pravaha.

## \|\| 57.8 \|\|

*nakṣatrasūryāś ca tathā grahatārāgaṇaiḥ saha \|*  
*unmukhābhimukhāḥ sarve cakrabhūtāḥ śritā divi \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Along with the planets and constellations, the sun and stars occupy the firmament in a circle looking upwards and sideways.

## \|\| 57.9 \|\|

*dhruveṇādhiṣṭhitāścaiva dhruvameva pradakṣiṇam \|*  
*prayānti ceśvaraṃ draṣṭuṃ meḍhībhūtaṃ dhruvaṃ divi \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Presided over (i.e. controlled) by Dhruva they circumambulate Dhruva. They move on in the firmament to see Lord Dhruva that acts like the pivot.

## \|\| 57.10 \|\|

*navayojanasāhasro viṣkambhaḥ savituḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*triguṇastasya vistāro maṇḍalasya pramāṇataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The diameter of the sun is nine thousand Yojanas. Its circular area is three times this.

## \|\| 57.11 \|\|

*dviguṇaḥ sūryavistārād vistāraḥ śaśinaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*tulyastayostu svarbhānur bhūtvādhastātprasarpati \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The extent of the moon is twice that of the Sun. Rāhu assumes a size equal to them and moves ahead beneath them.

## \|\| 57.12 \|\|

*uddhṛtya pṛthivīchāyāṃ nirmitāṃ maṇḍalākṛtim \|*  
*svarbhānostu bṛhatsthānaṃ tṛtīyaṃ yat tamomayam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The abode of Rāhu is full of darkness and is the third (one in size) because it is evolved out of the circular shadow of the earth.

## \|\| 57.13 \|\|

*candrasya ṣoḍaśo bhāgo bhārgavasya vidhīyate \|*  
*viṣkambhānmaṇḍalāccaiva yojanācca pramāṇataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The diameter, the circumference and the distance in yojanas of Bhargava (Venus) is a sixteenth part of that of the moon.

## \|\| 57.14-18 \|\|

*bhārgavātpādahīnastu vijñeyo vai bṛhaspatiḥ \|*  
*pādahīnau vakrasaurī tathāyāmapramāṇataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*vistārānmaṇḍalāccaiva pādahīnastayorbudhaḥ \|*  
*tārānakṣatrarūpāṇi vapuṣmantīha yāni vai \|\| 15 \|\|*

*budhena tāni tulyāni vistārānmaṇḍalādapi \|*  
*prāyaśaścandrayogīni vidyādṛkṣāṇi tattvavit \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tārānakṣatrarūpāṇi hīnāni tu parasparam \|*  
*śatāni pañca catvāri trīṇi dve caiva yojane \|\| 17 \|\|*

*sarvopari nikṛṣṭāni tārakāmaṇḍalāni tu \|*  
*yojanadvayamātrāṇi tebhyo hrasvaṃ na vidyate \|\| 18 \|\|*

14-18. Bṛhaspati (Jupiter) is of three-fourths of the size of Venus. Mars and Saturn are three-fourths of the size of Bṛhaspati. Budha (Mercury) is three-fourths of their size in extent and circumference. The stars and constellations, that have a body are equal to Budha in extent and circumference. The knower of truth must note that the stars that are in conjunction with the moon are ordinarily known as Ṛkṣas. The spheres of the comparatively smaller stars extend to five, four, three or two yojanas. Over all these there are still clusters of smaller stars which extend only to two hundred yojanas. There is none smaller than this.

## \|\| 57.19-20 \|\|

*upariṣṭāttrayasteṣāṃ grahā ye dūrasarpiṇaḥ \|*  
*sauro 'ṅgirāś ca vakraś ca jñeyā mandavicāriṇaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tebhyo 'dhastāttu catvāraḥ punaranye mahāgrahāḥ \|*  
*sūryaḥ somo budhaścaiva bhārgavaścaiva śīghragāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Over and above these starry spheres are the three planets viz., Saturn, Jupiter and Mars, which travel at a great distance from them. They should be known as slow-moving ones.

There are four other great planets beneath them, viz. the Sun, Moon, Mercury and Venus. They traverse quickly.

## \|\| 57.21 \|\|

*tāvantyastārakāḥ koṭyo yāvantyṛkṣāṇi sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*dhruvāt tu niyamāccaiṣām ṛkṣamārge vyavasthitiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Altogether there are as many crores of stars as there are constellations. They too are stationed in the orbit of constellations due to the restraining force of Dhruva.

## \|\| 57.22-26 \|\|

*saptāśvasyaiva sūryasya nīcoccatvamanukramāt \|*  
*uttarāyaṇamārgastho yadā parvasu candramāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*uccatvāddṛśyate śīghraṃ nātivyaktairgabhastibhiḥ \|*  
*tadā dakṣiṇamārgastho nīcāṃ vīthimupāśritaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*bhūmirekhāvṛtaḥ sūryaḥ paurṇimāvāsyayos tadā \|*  
*dadṛśe ca yathākālaṃ śīghramastamupaiti ca \|\| 24 \|\|*

*tasmāduttaramārgastho hy amāvāsyāṃ niśākaraḥ \|*  
*dadṛśe dakṣiṇe mārge niyamāddṛśyate na ca \|\| 25 \|\|*

*jyotiṣāṃ gatiyogena sūryasya tamasā vṛtaḥ \|*  
*samānakālāstamayau viṣuvatsu samodayau \|\| 26 \|\|*

22-26. The sun that has seven horses has an upper and a lower position by turns. When the sun is in his northern transit and when the moon, on the full moon nights, appears quickly because its position, is above, but the rays are not very clear, the moon (?) then is in the southern orbit that is lower. The sun. covered by the line of the earth on Full moon and New Moon days is seen, at the usual time, but it sets quickly. Hence on the New-Moon day the moon is in the northern orbit. It is invariably not seen, in the southern path on account of the movement of the planets and because it is enveloped by the shadow of the sun. On the equinotical days the sun and the moon rise and set simultaneously.

## \|\| 57.27-28 \|\|

*uttarāsu ca vīthīṣu vyantarāstamanodayau \|*  
*paurṇimāvāsyayor jñeyau jyotiścakrānuvartinau \|\| 27 \|\|*

*dakṣiṇāyanamārgastho yadā carati raśmivān \|*  
*grahāṇāṃ caiva sarveṣāṃ sūryo 'dhastāt prasarpati \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. In the northern orbits they rise and set without any difference in time on new moon and full moon days. They should then be known as following the groups of luminaries. When the sun is in the southern transit, it moves ahead beneath all other planets.

## \|\| 57.29 \|\|

*vistīrṇaṃ maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā tasyordhvaṃ carate śaśī*  
*nakṣatramaṇḍalaṃ kṛtsnaṃ somādūrdhvaṃ prasarpati \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Keeping his sphere wider the moon revolves above it (the sun). All the groups of constellations move above the moon.

## \|\| 57.30 \|\|

*nakṣatrebhyo budhaścordhvaṃ budhādūrdhvaṃ tu bhārgavaḥ \|*  
*vakrastu bhārgavādūrdhvaṃ vakrād ūrdhvaṃ bṛhaspatiḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Mercury is above all constellations; Venus is above Mercury. Mars is above Venus and Jupiter is above Mars.

## \|\| 57.31 \|\|

*tasmācchanaiścaraścordhvaṃ tasmātsaptarṣimaṇḍalam \|*  
*ṛṣīṇāṃ caiva saptānāṃ dhruvasyordhvaṃ vyavasthitiḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Saturn is above it. Above Saturn is the sphere of seven sages (Great Bear) and Dhruva(Pole Star) is stationed above the seven sages.

## \|\| 57.32-39 \|\|

*taṃ viṣṇulokaṃ paramaṃ jñātvā mucyeta kilbiṣāt \|*  
*dviguṇeṣu sahasreṣu yojanānāṃ śateṣu ca \|\| 32 \|\|*

*grahanakṣatratārāsu upariṣṭādyathākramam \|*  
*grahāś ca candrasūryau ca yutau divyena tejasā \|\| 33 \|\|*

*nityamṛkṣeṣu yujyante gacchanto 'harniśaṃ kramāt \|*  
*grahanakṣatrasūryās te nīcoccaṛjusaṃsthitāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*samāgame ca bhede ca paśyanti yugapatprajāḥ \|*  
*ṛtavaḥ ṣaṭ smṛtāḥ sarve samāgacchanti pañcadhā \|\| 35 \|\|*

*parasparāsthitā hyete yujyante ca parasparam \|*  
*asaṃkareṇa vijñeyas teṣāṃ yogastu vai budhaiḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*evaṃ saṃkṣipya kathitaṃ grahāṇāṃ gamanaṃ dvijāḥ \|*  
*bhāskarapramukhānāṃ ca yathādṛṣṭaṃ yathāśrutam \|\| 37 \|\|*

*grahādhipatye bhagavān brahmaṇā padmayoninā \|*  
*abhiṣiktaḥ sahasrāṃśū rudreṇa tu yathā guhaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tasmādgrahārcanā kāryā agnau codyaṃ yathāvidhi \|*  
*ādityagrahapīḍāyāṃ sadbhiḥ kāryārthasiddhaye \|\| 39 \|\|*

32-39. By knowing the region, of Viṣṇu, beyond all these, one is liberated from sin. Two hundred thousand Yojanas above Constellations, stars, the planets—Sun and Moon which are united with divine refulgence, move ahead day and night in due order. They come into contact with the constellations everyday. Hence they are sometimes stationed below, sometimes above and sometimes in a straight line. They glance at the subjects (below) simultaneously when in conjunction or when separated.

There are six seasons but of five distinct features. They overlap one another and their combination should, be understood by learned men without overlapping. O brahmins, thus the movement of planets has been succinctly mentioned in the case of the sun and other planets as I have heard and observed. The thousand-rayed lord Sun was crowned as the over-lord of planets by the lotus-born Brahmā, like Guha who was crowned by Rudra.

## Chapter 58 - Coronation of the Sun and others (sūryādi-abhiṣeka)

## \|\| 58.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*abhyaṣiñcatkathaṃ brahmā cādhipatye prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*devadaityamukhān sarvān sarvātmā vada sāṃpratam \|\| 1 \|\|*

The sages said:

1\. Tell us now how Brahmā Prajāpati, who is the soul of all, crowned as overlords, Devas, Daityas and others.

## \|\| 58.2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*grahādhipatye bhagavān abhyaṣiñcaddivākaram \|*  
*ṛkṣāṇāmoṣadhīnāṃ ca somaṃ brahmā prajāpatiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sūta said:

2\. Lord Brahma crowned the Sun as the overlord of planets. Brahmā, Prajāpati, crowned Soma (Moon) as the lord of constellations and medicinal herbs.

## \|\| 58.3 \|\|

*apāṃ ca varuṇaṃ devaṃ dhanānāṃ yakṣapuṅgavam \|*  
*ādityānāṃ tathā viṣṇuṃ vasūnāṃ pāvakaṃ tathā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. (He crowned) Varuṇa as the lord of the Waters; the leading Yakṣa (Kubera) as the lord of riches; Viṣṇu as the lord of Adityas; and Pāvaka (fire) as the lord of Vasus.

## \|\| 58.4 \|\|

*prajāpatīnāṃ dakṣaṃ ca marutāṃ śakrameva ca \|*  
*daityānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca prahlādaṃ daityapuṅgavam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. (He crowned) Dakṣa as the lord of Prajāpatis; Indra as the lord of Maruts; Prahlāda, the leading Daitya as the overlord of Daityas and Dānavas.

## \|\| 58.5 \|\|

*dharmaṃ pitṝṇām adhipaṃ nirṛtiṃ piśitāśinām \|*  
*rudraṃ paśūnāṃ bhūtānāṃ nandinaṃ gaṇanāyakam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. (He crowned) Dharma as the overlord of the Pitṛs; Nirṛti as the overlord of Rākṣasas; Rudra as the overlord of Paśus (Individual Souls) and Nandin, the leader of Gaṇas, as the overlord of Bhūtas (goblins).

## \|\| 58.6 \|\|

*vīrāṇāṃ vīrabhadraṃ ca piśācānāṃ bhayaṃkaram \|*  
*mātṝṇāṃ caiva cāmuṇḍāṃ sarvadevanamaskṛtām \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. (He crowned) Vīrabhadra as the overlord of heroes; Bhayaṅkara (the terrible one) as the overlord of Piśācas (ghosts); Cāmuṇḍā who is bowed to by Devas as the sovereign of Mothers.

## \|\| 58.7 \|\|

*rudrāṇāṃ devadeveśaṃ nīlalohitamīśvaram \|*  
*vighnānāṃ vyomajaṃ devaṃ gajāsyaṃ tu vināyakam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. (He crowned) lord Nīlalohita, lord of the chiefs of Devas, as the overlord of Rudras; the elephant-faced lord Vināyaka, born of Vyoman as the overlord of obstacles.

## \|\| 58.8 \|\|

*strīṇāṃ devīmumāṃ devīṃ vacasāṃ ca sarasvatīm \|*  
*viṣṇuṃ māyāvināṃ caiva svātmānaṃ jagatāṃ tathā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. (He crowned) goddess Umā as the sovereign of women; goddess Sarasvatī as the sovereign of speech; Viṣṇu as the overlord of the wielders of Māyā and himself as the overlord of the worlds.

## \|\| 58.9 \|\|

*himavantaṃ girīṇāṃ tu nadīnāṃ caiva jāhnavīm \|*  
*samudrāṇāṃ ca sarveṣām adhipaṃ payasāṃ nidhim \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. (He crowned) Himavat as the overlord of the mountains; the Ganges (born of sage Jahnu) as the sovereign of the rivers; and ocean the storehouse of the waters as the lord of all seas.

## \|\| 58.10-12 \|\|

*vṛkṣāṇāṃ caiva cāśvatthaṃ plakṣaṃ ca prapitāmahaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*gandharvavidyādharakinnarāṇām īśaṃ punaś citrarathaṃ cakāra \|*  
*nāgādhipaṃ vāsukimugravīryaṃ sarpādhipaṃ takṣakamugravīryam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*digvāraṇānāmadhipaṃ cakāra gajendram airāvatam ugravīryam /\**  
*suparṇamīśaṃ patatāmathāśvarājānamuccaiḥśravasaṃ cakāra \|\| 12 \|\|*

10-12. Brahmā crowned the Plakṣa and Aśvattha as the lords of trees; he made Citraratha the lord of Gandharvas, Vidyādharas and Kinnaras; Vāsuki of terrible vigour as the lord of Serpents and Takṣaka of terrible vigour as the lord of Sarpas (Cobras). He made the leading elephant Airāvata of terrible valour the lord of elephants. He made Garuḍa the lord of birds. He made Uccaiśśravas (the horse of Indra) the king of horses.

## \|\| 58.13 \|\|

*siṃhaṃ mṛgāṇāṃ vṛṣabhaṃ gavāṃ ca mṛgādhipānāṃ śarabhaṃ cakāra \|*  
*senādhipānāṃ guhamaprameyaṃ śrutismṛtīnāṃ lakulīśamīśam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. He made the lion the lord of animals; the bull the lord of the kine and Śarabha (the fabulous eight-footed beast) the lord of lions; the incomprehensible Guha the lord of all commanders-in-chief and Lakulīśa the lord of Śrutis and Smṛtis.

## \|\| 58.14 \|\|

*abhyaṣiñcatsudharmāṇaṃ tathā śaṅkhapadaṃ diśām \|*  
*ketumantaṃ krameṇaiva hemaromāṇameva ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. He made Sudharman, Śaṅkhapāla, Ketumān and Hemaroman the overlords of all quarters in order.

## \|\| 58.15 \|\|

*pṛthivyāṃ pṛthumīśānaṃ sarveṣāṃ tu maheśvaram \|*  
*caturmūrtiṣu sarvajñaṃ śaṅkaraṃ vṛṣabhadhvajam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. (He crowned) Pṛthu as the lord of the earth; Maheśvara as the lord of all; the bull-bannered omniscient lord Śaṅkara as the overlord among the four deities.

## \|\| 58.16 \|\|

*prasādādbhagavāñchambhoś cābhyaṣiñcadyathākramam \|*  
*purābhiṣicya puṇyātmā rarāja bhuvaneśvaraḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. By the grace of Śiva, the lord crowned these in due order. After crowning them at first the lord of the worlds felt fully satisfied.

## \|\| 58.17 \|\|

*etadvo vistareṇaiva kathitaṃ munipuṅgavāḥ \|*  
*abhiṣiktāstatastvete viśiṣṭā viśvayoninā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O leading sages, this has been mentioned to you in detail: These persons of special characteristics were all crowned by Lord Brahmā the source of origin of the universe.

## Chapter 59 - The form of solar rays (sūryaraśmi-svarūpa)

## \|\| 59.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etacchrutvā tu munayaḥ punastaṃ saṃśayānvitāḥ \|*  
*papracchuruttaraṃ bhūyas tadā te romaharṣaṇam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1\. On hearing this, the sages became overwhelmed with doubts and again asked Romaharṣaṇa.

## \|\| 59.2 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*yadetaduktaṃ bhavatā sūteha vadatāṃ vara \|*  
*etadvistarato brūhi jyotiṣāṃ ca vinirṇayam \|\| 2 \|\|*

The sages said:

2\. O Sūta, most excellent among the speakers, kindly tell us in detail the exact nature of the luminaries briefly.

## \|\| 59.3 \|\|

*śrutvā tu vacanaṃ teṣāṃ tadā sūtaḥ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*uvāca paramaṃ vākyaṃ teṣāṃ saṃśayanirṇaye \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. On hearing their words, Sūta of great concentration and purity spoke these weighty words in order to clear their doubts.

## \|\| 59.4 \|\|

*asminnarthe mahāprājñair yaduktaṃ śāntabuddhibhiḥ \|*  
*etadvo 'haṃ pravakṣyāmi sūryacandramasorgatim \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. In this matter I shall tell you what has already been stated by highly intelligent persons with tranquil wisdom. I shall recount the movement of the sun. and the moon.

## \|\| 59.5 \|\|

*fire-water-circle \|*  
*yathā devagṛhāṇīha sūryacandrādayo grahāḥ \|*  
*ataḥ paraṃ tu trividham agnervakṣye samudbhavam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. I shall tell you how the sun, the moon and other planets are the abodes of Devas. Thereafter, I shall mention the three types of fires and their origin.

## \|\| 59.6-9 \|\|

*divyasya bhautikasyāgner atho 'gneḥ pārthivasya ca \|*  
*vyuṣṭāyāṃ tu rajanyāṃ ca brahmaṇo 'vyaktajanmanaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*avyākṛtamidaṃ tvāsīn naiśena tamasā vṛtam \|*  
*caturbhāgāvaśiṣṭe 'smin loke naṣṭe viśeṣataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*svayaṃbhūrbhagavāṃstatra lokasarvārthasādhakaḥ \|*  
*khadyotavatsa vyacarad āvirbhāvacikīrṣayā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*so 'gniṃ sṛṣṭvātha lokādau pṛthivījalasaṃśritaḥ \|*  
*saṃhṛtya tatprakāśārthaṃ tridhā vyabhajadīśvaraḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

6-9. The three types of fire are: the divine fire, the elemental fire and the terrestrial fire.

When the night of Brahmā born of the unmanifest reached the stage of dawn, this visible universe was one that had not been analyzed. It was still enveloped in the nocturnal darkness. When the worlds were still in the state of destruction, when a fourth of the period still remained, the self-born, lord, he who achieves all the affairs of the worlds, moved about like a glowworm, with a desire to manifest. At the beginning of the world, he created. Agni (heat) in combination with earth and water. The Lord gathered these together to make it shine and then divided it into three.

## \|\| 59.10-11 \|\|

*pavano yastu loke 'smin pārthivo vahnirucyate \|*  
*yaścāsau lokādau sūrye śuciragnistu sa smṛtaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*vaidyuto 'bjastu vijñeyas teṣāṃ vakṣye tu lakṣaṇam \|*  
*vaidyuto jāṭharaḥ sauro vārigarbhāstrayo 'gnayaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. The fire in the world of mankind is called Pārthiva. The fire that blazes in the sun is called Śuci. The fire born of lightning is known as Abja (i.e. originating from the water portion). I shall now mention their characteristics. There are three types of fires with water within, viz., Vaidyuta, Jāṭhara (gastric) and Saura (Solar).

## \|\| 59.12-13 \|\|

*tasmādapaḥ pibansūryo gobhir dīpyatyasau vibhuḥ \|*  
*jale cābjaḥ samāviṣṭo nādbhir agniḥ praśāmyati \|\| 12 \|\|*

*mānavānāṃ ca kukṣistho nāgniḥ śāmyati pāvakaḥ \|*  
*arciṣmānpavanaḥ so 'gnir niṣprabho jāṭharaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. Hence, imbibing water through his rays the sun blazes (further). The Abja (waterborn—lightning) fire even when immersed in water is not quenched by it. The fire that is within the stomach of men is not put out by water. The gastric fire emits flames (i.e. heat), but is devoid of lustre.

## \|\| 59.14-19 \|\|

*yaścāyaṃ maṇḍalī śuklī nirūṣmā samprajāyate \|*  
*prabhā saurī tu pādena hy astaṃ yāte divākare \|\| 14 \|\|*

*agnimāviśate rātrau tasmāddūrātprakāśate \|*  
*udyantaṃ ca punaḥ sūryam auṣṇyam agneḥ samāviśet \|\| 15 \|\|*

*pādena pārthivasyāgnes tasmādagnistapatyasau \|*  
*prakāśoṣṇasvarūpe ca saurāgneye tu tejasī \|\| 16 \|\|*

*parasparānupraveśād āpyāyete parasparam \|*  
*uttare caiva bhūmyardhe tathā hyagniś ca dakṣiṇe \|\| 17 \|\|*

*uttiṣṭhati punaḥ sūryaḥ punarvai praviśaty apaḥ \|*  
*tasmāttāmrā bhavantyāpo divārātripraveśanāt \|\| 18 \|\|*

*astaṃ yāti punaḥ sūryo 'harvai praviśaty apaḥ \|*  
*tasmānnaktaṃ punaḥ śuklā āpo dṛśyanti bhāsvarāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

14-19. When the sun is setting, the solar lustre becomes a circular mass without heat and enters the fire at night through his rays. Hence the light of fire is seen even from a distance at night. The heat is transmitted to the sun from fire, when the sun rises. Only partially does the terrestrial fire enter the sun. Hence the fire continues to blaze. Thus the fire element in both terrestrial and solar fires contains heat and light. They penetrate mutually and develop each other. In the northern and southern hemispheres of the earth, the fire and the sun thus develop each other. The sun rises up from the waters and re-enters them. Therefore, due to this exit (from and into waters) by day and by night, the waters become copper-coloured. Again when the sun sets, the day (i.e. daylight) enters the waters. Hence at night, the waters are seen shining white.

## \|\| 59.20 \|\|

*etena kramayogena bhūmyardhe dakṣiṇottare \|*  
*udayāstamane nityam ahorātraṃ viśaty apaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. By means of this activity he enters waters perpetually, during day and night at the time of rising and setting both in the southern and northern hemispheres.

## \|\| 59.21 \|\|

*yaścāsau tapate sūryaḥ pibannaṃbho gabhastibhiḥ \|*  
*pārthivāgnivimiśro 'sau divyaḥ śuciriti smṛtaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The sun who blazes, imbibing the waters through his rays has the mixture of earthly and fiery particles within it. It is called divine fire.

## \|\| 59.22-23 \|\|

*sahasrapādasau vahnir vṛttakumbhanibhaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*ādatte sa tu nāḍīnāṃ sahasreṇa samantataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*nādeyīścaiva sāmudrīḥ kūpāścaiva tathā ghanāḥ \|*  
*sthāvarā jaṅgamāścaiva vāpīkulyādikā apaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. This fire (i.e. sun) has a thousand feet (i.e. rays). It is like a circular pot. It takes up waters from various waterresorts through the thousand tubular rays. It takes waters from the rivers, seas, wells, clouds etc. It takes up both mobile and immobile waters i.e. those of the canals and tanks.

## \|\| 59.24-25 \|\|

*classes of sunrays \|*  
*tasya raśmisahasraṃ tac chītavarṣoṣṇaniḥsravam \|*  
*tāsāṃ catuḥśatā nāḍyo varṣante citramūrtayaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*bhajanāścaiva mālyāś ca ketanāḥ patanās tathā \|*  
*amṛtā nāmataḥ sarvā raśmayo vṛṣṭisarjanāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. He has a thousand rays emitting snow, rain and heat. Of them four hundred tubular rays have forms of variegated colours. They shower rain. Their collective name is Amṛta and the several individual names are Bhajanas, Mālyas, Ketanas and Patanas.

## \|\| 59.26-29 \|\|

*himodvahāś ca tā nāḍyo raśmayas triśatāḥ punaḥ \|*  
*reśā meghāś ca vātsyāś ca hlādinyo himasarjanāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*candrabhā nāmataḥ sarvā pītābhāś ca gabhastayaḥ \|*  
*śuklāś ca kakubhāścaiva gāvo viśvabhṛtas tathā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*śuklāstā nāmataḥ sarvās triśatīrgharmasarjanāḥ \|*  
*somo bibharti tābhistu manuṣyapitṛdevatāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*manuṣyānauṣadheneha svadhayā ca pitṝnapi \|*  
*amṛtena surān sarvāṃs tisṛbhis tarpayatyasau \|\| 29 \|\|*

26-27a. The tubular rays carrying and emitting snow are three hundred in number. The several names of these rays emitting snow are Reśas, Meghas, Vātsyas and Hlādinīs. Their collective name is Candrabhā and they are yellow in lustre.

27b-28a. Śukla \[śuklaḥ\], Kakubha \[kakubhaḥ\] and Viśvabhṛt are the individual names of the rays emitting heat; their collective name is also Śukla.

28b-29. The moon sustains human beings, Pitṛs and Devas through them (the above rays).

He propitiates human beings through the medicinal herbs; the Pitṛs with Svadhā and Devas through nectar.

## \|\| 59.30-38 \|\|

*vasante caiva grīṣme ca śataiḥ sa tapate tribhiḥ \|*  
*varṣāsvatho śaradi ca caturbhiḥ saṃpravarṣati \|\| 30 \|\|*

*hemante śiśire caiva himamutsṛjate tribhiḥ \|*  
*Götter in der Sonneindro dhātā bhagaḥ pūṣā mitro 'tha varuṇo 'ryamā \|\| 31 \|\|*

*aṃśur vivasvāṃstvaṣṭā ca parjanyo viṣṇureva ca \|*  
*varuṇo māghamāse tu sūrya eva tu phālgune \|\| 32 \|\|*

*caitre māsi bhavedaṃśur dhātā vaiśākhatāpanaḥ \|*  
*jyeṣṭhe māsi bhavedindra āṣāḍhe cāryamā raviḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*vivasvān śrāvaṇe māsi prauṣṭhapade bhagaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*parjanyo 'śvayuje māsi tvaṣṭā vai kārtike raviḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*mārgaśīrṣe bhavenmitraḥ pauṣe viṣṇuḥ sanātanaḥ \|*  
*pañcaraśmisahasrāṇi varuṇasyārkakarmaṇi \|\| 35 \|\|*

*ṣaḍbhiḥ sahasraiḥ pūṣā tu devo 'ṃśuḥ saptabhis tathā \|*  
*dhātāṣṭabhiḥ sahasraistu navabhistu śatakratuḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*vivasvān daśabhir yāti yātyekādaśabhir bhagaḥ \|*  
*saptabhistapate mitras tvaṣṭā caivāṣṭabhiḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*aryamā daśabhir yāti parjanyo navabhis tathā \|*  
*ṣaḍbhī raśmisahasraistu viṣṇustapati medinīm \|\| 38 \|\|*

30-31a. During spring and summer the sun blazes by his three hundred rays. During the rainy season and Autumn he showers rains through the four hundred tubular rays. During the early and the late winter he discharges snow through his three hundred rays.

31b-35a. The twelve suns are Indra, Dhātṛ, Bhaga, Pūṣan, Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman, Aṃśu, Vivasvān, Tvaṣṭṛ, Parjanya and Viṣṇu.

Varuṇa is the sun in Māgha; Pūṣan in the Phālguna. In the month of Caitra, Aṃśu is the sun. Dhātṛ is the sun in Vaiśākha. In Jyeṣṭha Indra is the sun. In Āṣāḍha, the sun is Aryaman. Vivasvan is the sun in Śrāvaṇa. In Bhādra the sun is Bhaga. Parjanya is the sun in Āśvina. Tvaṣṭṛ is the sun in Kārttika. In Mārgaśīrṣa Mitra is the sun and Viṣṇu is the sun in Pauṣa.

35b-38. While performing the duty of the sun, Varuṇa has five thousand rays; Pūṣan six thousand rays; Aṃśu seven thousand rays; Dhātṛ eight thousand rays; Indra nine thousand rays; Vivasvān ten thousand rays; Bhaga eleven thousand rays; Mitra seven thousand rays; Tvaṣṭṛ eight thousand rays; Aryaman ten thousand rays; Parjanya nine thousand rays; Viṣṇu scorches the earth with six thousand rays.

## \|\| 59.39-40 \|\|

*vasaṃte kapilaḥ sūryo grīṣme kāñcanasaprabhaḥ \|*  
*śveto varṣāsu varṇena pāṇḍuḥ śaradi bhāskaraḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*hemante tāmravarṇastu śiśire lohito raviḥ \|*  
*iti varṇāḥ samākhyātā mayā sūryasamudbhavāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. In the spring the sun is tawny coloured; in the summer he has the lustre of gold. During the rainy season the colour of the sun is white. In the autumn the sun is greycoloured. In the early winter the sun is copper-coloured and in the late winter he is red in colour.

## \|\| 59.41-45 \|\|

*oṣadhīṣu balaṃ dhatte svadhayā ca pitṛṣvapi \|*  
*sūryo 'mareṣvapyamṛtaṃ trayaṃ triṣu niyacchati \|\| 41 \|\|*

*evaṃ raśmisahasraṃ tat sauraṃ lokārthasādhakam \|*  
*bhidyate lokamāsādya jalaśītoṣṇaniḥsravam \|\| 42 \|\|*

*ityetanmaṇḍalaṃ śuklaṃ bhāsvaraṃ sūryasaṃjñitam \|*  
*nakṣatragrahasomānāṃ pratiṣṭhāyonireva ca \|\| 43 \|\|*

*candraṛkṣagrahāḥ sarve vijñeyāḥ sūryasaṃbhavāḥ \|*  
*nakṣatrādhipatiḥ somo nayanaṃ vāmamīśituḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*nayanaṃ caivam īśasya dakṣiṇaṃ bhāskaraḥ svayam \|*  
*teṣāṃ janānāṃ loke 'smin nayanaṃ nayate yataḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

41-45. The sun infuses strength into the medicinal herbs; he propitiates the Pitṛs by means of Svadhā rays; he instils nectar into the immortal beings. Thus, he imparts three things to the three groups.

The thousand rays of the sun serve the purpose of the world. Reaching the earth they assume different forms by emitting snow, rain and heat. Thus the sphere of the sun is white and is named after him. He is the support and source of origin of the stars, planets and the moon.

## Chapter 60 - The Solar Sphere

## \|\| 60.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*śeṣāḥ pañca grahā jñeyā īśvarāḥ kāmacāriṇaḥ \|*  
*paṭhyate cāgnirāditya udakaṃ candramāḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1\. It is cited that the sun is fire and the moon is water. The other five planets are known as lords who move about as they please.

## \|\| 60.2 \|\|

*śeṣāṇāṃ prakṛtiṃ samyag vakṣyamāṇāṃ nibodhata \|*  
*surasenāpatiḥ skandaḥ paṭhyate 'ṅgārako grahaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Understand the source of origin of the remaining planets which is clearly being recounted now. It is cited that the planet Mars is Skanda (Karttikeya) the commander-in-chief of the army of Devas.

## \|\| 60.3-5 \|\|

*nārāyaṇaṃ budhaṃ prāhur devaṃ jñānavido janāḥ \|*  
*sarvalokaprabhuḥ sākṣād yamo lokaprabhuḥ svayam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*mahāgraho dvijaśreṣṭhā mandagāmī śanaiścaraḥ \|*  
*devāsuragurū dvau tu bhānumantau mahāgrahau \|\| 4 \|\|*

*prajāpatisutāvuktau tataḥ śukrabṛhaspatī*  
*ādityamūlamakhilaṃ trailokyaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

3-5. People of perfect knowledge say that Mercury is lord Nārāyaṇa. O excellent brahmins, the great planet Śanaiścara, the slow-moving Saturn is Yama, the lord of the worlds. The preceptors of Devas and Asuras are the great planets Venus and Jupiter with (refulgent) rays. They are mentioned as the sons of Prajāpati.

There is no doubt that the three worlds have their source in the sun.

## \|\| 60.6-8 \|\|

*bhavatyasmājjagatkṛtsnaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam \|*  
*rudrendropendracandrāṇāṃ viprendrāgnidivaukasām \|\| 6 \|\|*

*dyutirdyutimatāṃ kṛtsnaṃ yattejaḥ sarvalaukikam \|*  
*sarvātmā sarvalokeśo mahādevaḥ prajāpatiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*sūrya eva trilokeśo mūlaṃ paramadaivatam \|*  
*tataḥ saṃjāyate sarvaṃ tatraiva pravilīyate \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. The entire universe including Devas, Asuras and human beings originates from him. He is the lustre of all luminaries and the universal refulgence. The refulgence of Rudra, Indra, Upendra, the moon, the leading brahmins, the fire and the heaven-dwellers comes from the sun. He is the soul of all. He is the lord of all worlds. He alone is Mahādeva, Prajāpati and the lord of the three worlds. He is the original great deity. Everything originates from him and dissolves in him.

## \|\| 60.9 \|\|

*bhāvābhāvau hi lokānām ādityānniḥsṛtau purā \|*  
*avijñeyo graho viprā dīptimānsuprabho raviḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The existence and non-existence of the worlds originated from the sun formerly. O brahmins, this refulgent sun of great lustre is an incomprehensible planet.

## \|\| 60.10-11 \|\|

*atra gacchanti nidhanaṃ jāyante ca punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*kṣaṇā muhūrtā divasā niśāḥ pakṣāś ca kṛtsnaśaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*māsāḥ saṃvatsaraścaiva ṛtavo 'tha yugāni ca \|*  
*tadādityādṛte hyeṣā kālasaṃkhyā na vidyate \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. All these units of time begin from him and end in him again and again, viz., kṣaṇas (moments), muhūrtas (a unit of 48 mts.), days, nights, fortnights, months, years, seasons and yugas. Hence without the sun there is no reckoning of time.

## \|\| 60.12-15 \|\|

*kālādṛte na niyamo na dīkṣā nāhnikakramaḥ \|*  
*ṛtūnāṃ ca vibhāgaś ca puṣpaṃ mūlaṃ phalaṃ kutaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*kutaḥ sasyaviniṣpattis tṛṇauṣadhigaṇo 'pi ca \|*  
*abhāvo vyavahārāṇāṃ jantūnāṃ divi ceha ca \|\| 13 \|\|*

*jagatpratāpanamṛte bhāskaraṃ rudrarūpiṇam \|*  
*sa eṣa kālaścāgniś ca dvādaśātmā prajāpatiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tapatyeṣa dvijaśreṣṭhās trailokyaṃ sacarācaram \|*  
*sa eṣa tejasāṃ rāśiḥ samastaḥ sārvalaukikaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

12-15. Without Kāla (time) there is no order, no initiation, no daily ritual. How can there be the division of the seasons? Whence are these flowers, roots and fruits? Whence is the outcome of plants? How can there be the different kinds of grass and medicinal plants? The dealings of the creatures in heaven and here too will be non-existent without the sun who is the form of Rudra, the scorcher of the universe. He alone is time, fire, Dvādaśātman (one having twelve forms) and Prajāpati. O excellent brahmins, he scorches the three worlds including the mobile and immobile beings. He is the mine of splendour. He is all in all, the whole set of worlds.

## \|\| 60.16 \|\|

*uttamaṃ mārgamāsthāya rātryahobhir idaṃ jagat \|*  
*pārśvata ūrdhvam adhaś caiva tāpayatyeṣa sarvaśaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Adopting the excellent path, he scorches the entire universe from the sides, from above and from below in the course of nights and days.

## \|\| 60.17 \|\|

*yathā prabhākaro dīpo gṛhamadhye 'valambitaḥ \|*  
*pārśvata ūrdhvam adhaścaiva tamo nāśayate samam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. If a bright lamp is hung in the middle of the house, it dispels darkness from the sides, the portion above and the portion below, at the same time.

## \|\| 60.18 \|\|

*tadvatsahasrakiraṇo graharājo jagatprabhuḥ \|*  
*sūryo gobhir jagat sarvam ādīpayati sarvataḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. In the same manner the thousand-rayed sun, the king of planets, the lord of the universe, illuminates the entire universe by means of his rays.

## \|\| 60.19 \|\|

*7 special sunrays \|*  
*rave raśmisahasraṃ yat prāṅmayā samudāhṛtam \|*  
*teṣāṃ śreṣṭhāḥ punaḥ sapta raśmayo grahayonayaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Seven rays, that are the source of origin of the planets are the most excellent ones among the thousand, rays mentioned by me before.

## \|\| 60.20-21 \|\|

*suṣumno harikeśaś ca viśvakarmā tathaiva ca \|*  
*viśvavyacāḥ punaścādyaḥ saṃnaddhaś ca tataḥ paraḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*sarvāvasuḥ punaścānyaḥ svarāḍanyaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*suṣumnaḥ sūryaraśmistu dakṣiṇāṃ rāśim aidhayat \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. They are Suṣumna, Harikeśa, Viśvakarman, Viśvavyacas, Sannaddha, Sarvāvasu and Svarāṭ.

The sun’s ray Suṣumna makes the southern region flourish. Suṣumna is glorified as the ray that moves about above, below and on the sides.

## \|\| 60.22-26 \|\|

*nyagūrdhvādhaḥ pracāro 'sya suṣumnaḥ parikīrtitaḥ \|*  
*harikeśaḥ purastād yo ṛkṣayoniḥ prakīrtyate \|\| 22 \|\|*

*dakṣiṇe viśvakarmā ca raśmirvardhayate budham \|*  
*viśvavyacāstu yaḥ paścāc chukrayoniḥ smṛto budhaiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*saṃnaddhaś ca tu yo raśmiḥ sa yonir lohitasya tu \|*  
*ṣaṣṭhaḥ sarvāvasū raśmiḥ sa yonistu bṛhaspateḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*śanaiścaraṃ punaś cāpi raśmir āpyāyate svarāṭ \|*  
*evaṃ sūryaprabhāvena nakṣatragrahatārakāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*dṛśyante divi tāḥ sarvāḥ viśvaṃ cedaṃ punarjagat \|*  
*na kṣīyante yatastāni tasmānnakṣatratā smṛtā \|\| 26 \|\|*

22-26. Harikeśa which is in front (in the east) is glorified as the source of origin of constellations. In the south, the ray Viśvakarmā develops Budha (Mercury). The ray Viśvavyacas which is in the west (behind) is the source of origin of Śukra (Venus). The ray Sannaddha is the source of origin of Mars. The ray Sarvāvasu is the source of origin of Bṛhaspati (Jupiter). The ray Svarāṭ nourishes Śanaiścara (Saturn). Thus it is due to the power of the sun that the constellations, planets and stars are seen in the heaven. This entire universe is sustained by him. The constellations are called Nakṣatras. The word is derived from √kṣi with the prohibitive particle ‘na’ i.e. \[na kṣīyante\] (i.e. those which do not perish).

## Chapter 61 - The situation of the planets (graha-saṃkhyā)

## \|\| 61.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*kṣetrāṇyetāni sarvāṇi ātapanti gabhastibhiḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ kṣetrāṇyathādatte sūryo nakṣatratārakāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*cīrṇena sukṛteneha sukṛtānte grahāśrayāḥ \|*  
*tāraṇāttārakā hyetāḥ śuklatvāccaiva tārakāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. All these are the abodes which blaze by means of solar rays. The constellations and stars are the abodes to be attained by merits. They are called Tārakas because they enable people to cross the ocean of worldly existence and also because they are white.

## \|\| 61.3 \|\|

*divyānāṃ pārthivānāṃ ca naiśānāṃ caiva sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*ādānānnityamādityas tejasāṃ tamasāmapi \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The sun is called Āditya because he takes up the divine and terrestrial splendours as well as the nocturnal darkness.

## \|\| 61.4 \|\|

*savane syandane 'rthe ca dhātur eṣa vibhāṣyate \|*  
*savanāttejaso 'pāṃ ca tenāsau savitā mataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The root ‘su’ is used in two meanings to extract juice or to flow. Since the sun extracts refulgence and makes water flow, it is called Savitṛ.

## \|\| 61.5 \|\|

*bahulaścandra ityeṣa hlādane dhāturucyate \|*  
*śuklatve cāmṛtatve ca śītatve ca vibhāvyate \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The root ‘cadi’ from which the word Candra is derived means ‘to delight’. It implies whiteness, chillness, and nectarine nature of the moon (Candra).

## \|\| 61.6 \|\|

*sūryācandramasordivye maṇḍale bhāsvare khage \|*  
*jalatejomaye śukle vṛttakuṃbhanibhe śubhe \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The divine discs of the sun and the moon are refulgent. They move in the sky. They are white and are of the nature of fire and water. They are splendid and they resemble a circular pot.

## \|\| 61.7 \|\|

*ghanatoyātmakaṃ tatra maṇḍalaṃ śaśinaḥ smṛtam \|*  
*ghanatejomayaṃ śuklaṃ maṇḍalaṃ bhāskarasya tu \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The disc of the moon is of the nature of dense water. The disc of the sun is white and is of the nature of dense fire.

## \|\| 61.8 \|\|

*vasanti sarvadevāś ca sthānānyetāni sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*manvantareṣu sarveṣu ṛkṣasūryagrahāśrayāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Devas reside in constellations, sun and planets. They live everywhere in these abodes in all the manvantaras.

## \|\| 61.9 \|\|

*tena grahā gṛhāṇyeva tadākhyāste bhavanti ca \|*  
*sauraṃ sūryo 'viśatsthānaṃ saumyaṃ somastathaiva ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Hence the planets are abodes named after their respective planets. The Sun entered the abode Saura. The Moon entered the abode Saumya.

## \|\| 61.10 \|\|

*śaukraṃ śukro 'viśatsthānaṃ ṣoḍaśārciḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*bṛhad bṛhaspatiścaiva lohitaścaiva lohitam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Venus entered the abode Śaukra. Jupiter, the valorous, with sixteen rays entered the abode Bṛhad (big). The Mars entered the abode Lohita pertaining to Mars.

## \|\| 61.11 \|\|

*śanaiścaraṃ tathā sthānaṃ devaścāpi śanaiścaraḥ \|*  
*baudhaṃ budhastu svarbhānuḥ svarbhānusthānamāśritaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The Saturn entered the abode Śanaiścara. The Mercury entered the abode Baudha. The evil planet Rāhu entered the abode Svarbhānu (named after him).

## \|\| 61.12 \|\|

*nakṣatrāṇi ca sarvāṇi nakṣatrāṇi viśanti ca \|*  
*gṛhāṇyetāni sarvāṇi jyotīṃṣi sukṛtātmanām \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The deities of constellations entered all these abodes. These luminaries are the abodes of meritorious souls.

## \|\| 61.13 \|\|

*kalpādau sampravṛttāni nirmitāni svayaṃbhuvā \|*  
*sthānānyetāni tiṣṭhanti yāvad ābhūtasaṃplavam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. These abodes have been created by the self-born deity. They began to function at the beginning of kalpa and they stay until all the living beings are dissolved.

## \|\| 61.14 \|\|

*manvantareṣu sarveṣu devasthānāni tāni vai \|*  
*abhimānino 'vatiṣṭhante devāḥ sthānaṃ punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. In all the manvantaras they alone are the abodes of Devas. These deities who have identified themselves with the abodes occupy these divine abodes again and again.

## \|\| 61.15-20 \|\|

*atītaistu sahaitāni bhāvyābhāvyaiḥ suraiḥ saha \|*  
*vartante vartamānaiś ca sthānibhistaiḥ suraiḥ saha \|\| 15 \|\|*

*asminmanvantare caiva grahā vaimānikāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*vivasvānaditeḥ putraḥ sūryo vaivasvate 'ntare \|\| 16 \|\|*

*dyutimānṛṣiputrastu somo devo vasuḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*śukro devastu vijñeyo bhārgavo 'surayājakaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*bṛhattejāḥ smṛto devo devācāryo 'ṅgiraḥsutaḥ \|*  
*budho manoharaścaiva ṛṣiputrastu sa smṛtaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*śanaiścaro virūpastu saṃjñāputro vivasvataḥ \|*  
*agnirvikeśyāṃ jajñe tu yuvāsau lohitārciṣaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*nakṣatraṛkṣanāminyo dākṣāyaṇyastu tāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*svarbhānuḥ siṃhikāputro bhūtasaṃtāpano 'suraḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

15-20. They occupy these abodes along with Devas of the past, present and future. In this current manvantara the planets are moving about in aerial chariots.

In the Vaivasvata manvantara the sun is Vivasvān the son of Aditi; the lustrous lord Moon the son of sage Atri; lord Śukra, Bhārgava, is known as the priest of Asuras.

The preceptor of Devas, the shining one of massive splendour, is the son of Aṅgiras (Bṛhaspati). Budha (Mercury) is the charming son of a sage. Saturn is the ugly son of Vivasvān born of Saṃjñā. Agni was born of Vikeśī as the youthful son of Lohitārchis. The constellations named Nakṣatra and Ṛkṣa are Dākṣāyaṇīs (daughters of Dakṣa). Rāhu is the son of Siṃhikā. He is an Asura causing distress to living beings.

## \|\| 61.21 \|\|

*somarkṣagrahasūryeṣu kīrtitāstvabhimāninaḥ \|*  
*sthānānyetānyathoktāni sthāninyaścaiva devatāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Thus the constellations and planets in the sun and the moon as also their abodes and the various deities occupying them have all been mentioned.

## \|\| 61.22 \|\|

*sauram agnimayaṃ sthānaṃ sahasrāṃśorvivasvataḥ \|*  
*himāṃśostu smṛtaṃ sthānam ammayaṃ śuklameva ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The fiery abode Saura belongs to the thousand-rayed Vivasvān. The abode of the snow-rayed moon is watery and white.

## \|\| 61.23 \|\|

*āpyaṃ śyāmaṃ manojñaṃ ca budharaśmigṛhaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*śuklasyāpyammayaṃ śuklaṃ padaṃ ṣoḍaśaraśmivat \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The abode of Budha (mercury) is watery, dark-coloured and charming. The region of Śukra (Venus) is also watery but white with sixteen rays.

## \|\| 61.24 \|\|

*navaraśmi tu bhaumasya lohitaṃ sthānam uttamam \|*  
*haridrābhaṃ bṛhaccāpi ṣoḍaśārcirbṛhaspateḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The abode of Bhauma (Mars) is reddish and it has nine rays. The abode of Bṛhaspati (Jupiter) is yellow with sixteen rays and is very large.

## \|\| 61.25 \|\|

*aṣṭaraśmigṛhaṃ cāpi proktaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ śanaiścare \|*  
*svarbhānostāmasaṃ sthānaṃ bhūtasaṃtāpanālayam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The abode Śani (Saturn) is black with eight rays. The abode of Svarbhānu (Rāhu) is gloomy and is a place of great distress to living beings.

## \|\| 61.26 \|\|

*vijñeyāstārakāḥ sarvās tv ṛṣayastvekaraśmayaḥ \|*  
*āśrayāḥ puṇyakīrtīnāṃ śuklāścāpi svavarṇataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. All the stars should be known as the abodes of sages with one ray each. They are the resorts of men of meritorious renown and are white in colour.

## \|\| 61.27 \|\|

*ghanatoyātmikā jñeyāḥ kalpādāveva nirmitāḥ \|*  
*ādityaraśmisaṃyogāt saṃprakāśātmikāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. They are of the nature of dense water (snow). They were created in the beginning of the kalpa. Thanks to the contact with the rays of the sun they have a shining appearance.

## \|\| 61.28 \|\|

*navayojanasāhasro viṣkaṃbhaḥ savituḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*triguṇastasya vistāro maṇḍalasya pramāṇataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The diameter of the sun is nine thousand yojanas. The extent of its circular surface is three times that.

## \|\| 61.29 \|\|

*dviguṇaḥ sūryavistārād vistāraḥ śaśinaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*tulyastayostu svarbhānur bhūtvādhastātprasarpati \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The extent of the moon is twice that of the sun. Rāhu assumes a form equal to both of them and moves about beneath them.

## \|\| 61.30 \|\|

*uddhṛtya pṛthivīchāyāṃ nirmitāṃ maṇḍalākṛtim \|*  
*svarbhānostu bṛhatsthānaṃ tṛtīyaṃ yattamomayam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The third massive abode of Rāhu is dark and dreary. It is created in the form of a circle out of the shadow of the earth.

## \|\| 61.31-33 \|\|

*ādityāttacca niṣkramya samaṃ gacchati parvasu \|*  
*ādityameti somācca punaḥ saureṣu parvasu \|\| 31 \|\|*

*svarbhānuṃ nudate yasmāt tasmātsvarbhānurucyate \|*  
*candrasya ṣoḍaśo bhāgo bhārgavasya vidhīyate \|\| 32 \|\|*

*viṣkaṃbhānmaṇḍalāccaiva yojanāgrātpramāṇataḥ \|*  
*bhārgavātpādahīnastu vijñeyo vai bṛhaspatiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

31-32a. Setting out from the sun during the parvan days it goes to the moon. Again during the solar parvan days it goes to the sun from the moon. Since Rāhu pushes and prompts the sun in the heaven it is called Svarbhānu.

32b-33. The diameter, circumference and distance in terms of yojanas of Venus is a sixteenth part of that of the moon. Jupiter is three-fourths of the size of Venus.

## \|\| 61.34 \|\|

*bṛhaspateḥ pādahīnau vakrasaurī ubhau smṛtau \|*  
*vistārānmaṇḍalāccaiva pādahīnastayorbudhaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Mars and Saturn are a fourth less than Jupiter. In extent and width Mercury is a fourth less than these two.

## \|\| 61.35 \|\|

*tārānakṣatrarūpāṇi vapuṣmantīha yāni vai \|*  
*budhena tāni tulyāni vistārānmaṇḍalācca vai \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The forms of those constellations and stars that are embodied are equal to Mercury in width and circular area.

## \|\| 61.36-39 \|\|

*prāyaśaścandrayogīni vidyādṛkṣāṇi tattvavit \|*  
*tārānakṣatrarūpāṇi hīnāni tu parasparam \|\| 36 \|\|*

*śatāni pañca catvāri trīṇi dve caiva yojane \|*  
*sarvopari nikṛṣṭāni tārakāmaṇḍalāni tu \|\| 37 \|\|*

*yojanānyardhamātrāṇi tebhyo hrasvaṃ na vidyate \|*  
*upariṣṭāttrayasteṣāṃ grahāste dūrasarpiṇaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*sauro 'ṅgirāś ca vakraś ca jñeyā mandavicāriṇaḥ \|*  
*pūrvameva samākhyātā gatisteṣāṃ yathākramam \|\| 39 \|\|*

36-39. The constellations that are in conjunction with the moon are ordinarily known as Ṛkṣas. The spheres of the comparatively smaller stars are five, four, three or two yojanas. Over all these there are clusters of still smaller stars which extend to only half a yojana in width. There is none smaller than this. Over and above these starry spheres are the three planets which move at a great distance from them. They should be known as slow moving ones. The speed of these has already been mentioned in due order.

## \|\| 61.40-45 \|\|

*eteṣveva grahāḥ sarve nakṣatreṣu samutthitāḥ \|*  
*vivasvānaditeḥ putraḥ sūryo vai munisattamāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*viśākhāsu samutpanno grahāṇāṃ prathamo grahaḥ \|*  
*tviṣimān dharmaputrastu somo devo vasustu saḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*śītaraśmiḥ samutpannaḥ kṛttikāsu niśākaraḥ \|*  
*ṣoḍaśārcirbhṛgoḥ putraḥ śukraḥ sūryādanantaram \|\| 42 \|\|*

*tārāgrahāṇāṃ pravaras tiṣye kṣetre samutthitaḥ \|*  
*grahaścāṅgirasaḥ putro dvādaśārcirbṛhaspatiḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*phālgunīṣu samutpannaḥ pūrvākhyāsu jagadguruḥ \|*  
*navārcirlohitāṅgaś ca prajāpatisuto grahaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*āṣāḍhāsviha pūrvāsu samutpanna iti smṛtaḥ \|*  
*revatīṣveva saptārciḥsthāne sauriḥ śanaiścaraḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

40-45. All the planets are born of constellations. O excellent sages, the sun, the son of Aditi, the first among the planets, is born of the constellation Viśākhā. The lustrous son of Dharma, lord Vasu, Soma (moon), the cool-rayed lord of the night, is born of the constellation Kṛttikā. The sixteen-rayed son of Bhṛgu, Śukra (Venus) who is the most excellent among the stars and planets after the sun, is born of the constellation Tiṣya. The planet Bṛhaspati (Jupiter), the twelve-rayed son of Aṅgiras, the preceptor of the universe, is born of the constellation Pūrvaphālgunī.

The planet (Mars) son of Prajāpati, the nine-rayed red bodied planet is born of the constellation Pūrvāṣāḍhā.

The son of sun, the seven-rayed Saturn, was born of the constellation Revatī.

## \|\| 61.46-47 \|\|

*saumyo budho dhaniṣṭhāsu pañcārcir udito grahaḥ \|*  
*tamomayo mṛtyusutaḥ prajākṣayakaraḥ śikhī \|\| 46 \|\|*

*āśleṣāsu samutpannaḥ sarvahārī mahāgrahaḥ \|*  
*tathā svanāmadheyeṣu dākṣāyaṇyaḥ samutthitāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. The five-rayed planet Budha (Mercury) the son of the moon is born of the constellation Dhaniṣṭhā.

Śikhī (Ketu) the great planet that destroys all, who is dark in nature, who is the son of Mṛtyu the god of Death and who is the cause of destruction of the subjects, is born of the constellation Āsleṣā. Dakṣa’s daughters were born of the constellations which have their own names.

## \|\| 61.48 \|\|

*tamovīryamayo rāhuḥ prakṛtyā kṛṣṇamaṇḍalaḥ \|*  
*bharaṇīṣu samutpanno grahaścandrārkamardanaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Dark-sphered Rāhu who is full of Tāmasaic vigour, is the planet that suppresses the moon and the sun. He is born of the constellation Bharaṇī

## \|\| 61.49-50 \|\|

*ete tārā grahāścāpi boddhavyā bhārgavādayaḥ \|*  
*janmanakṣatrapīḍāsu yānti vaiguṇyatāṃ yataḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*mucyate tena doṣeṇa tatastadgrahabhaktitaḥ \|*  
*sarvagrahāṇāmeteṣām ādirāditya ucyate \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. It should be noted that the planets beginning with Bhārgava (Venus) are known as star-planets (i.e planets resembling stars). Persons who are affected by afflictions from their birthday stars are liberated from that defect by devotion to their respective planets. Among all the planets the first one, it is said, is Āditya (Sun).

## \|\| 61.51-54 \|\|

*tārāgrahāṇāṃ śukrastu ketūnāṃ cāpi dhūmavān \|*  
*dhruvaḥ kila grahāṇāṃ tu vibhaktānāṃ caturdiśam \|\| 51 \|\|*

*nakṣatrāṇāṃ śraviṣṭhā syād ayanānāṃ tathottaram \|*  
*varṣāṇāṃ caiva pañcānām ādyaḥ saṃvatsaraḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*ṛtūnāṃ śiśiraścāpi māsānāṃ māgha ucyate \|*  
*pakṣāṇāṃ śuklapakṣastu tithīnāṃ pratipattathā \|\| 53 \|\|*

*ahorātravibhāgānām ahaścādiḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*muhūrtānāṃ tathaivādir muhūrto rudradaivataḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

51-54. Among all the star-planets Śukra is the first. Among all the Ketus (flag-like Meteors) the smoky one is the first. (It is usually called Dhūmaketu). Dhruva is the first among the planets distributed in all the four quarters. Among constellations the first is Śraviṣṭhā. Among the Ayanas (transits) the Uttarāyaṇa (northern transit) is the first. Among the five years the first is Saṃvatsara. Among the seasons it is the late winter (śiśira). Among the months it is Māgha. Among the fortnights it is the bright half and among Tithis it is Pratipat (first day). Among the division of days and nights, the day is the first. The first of the muhūrtas is that the deity of which is Rudra.

## \|\| 61.55-58 \|\|

*kṣaṇaścāpi nimeṣādiḥ kālaḥ kālavidāṃ varāḥ \|*  
*śravaṇāntaṃ dhaniṣṭhādi yugaṃ syātpañcavārṣikam \|\| 55 \|\|*

*bhānorgativiśeṣeṇa cakravatparivartate \|*  
*divākaraḥ smṛtastasmāt kālakṛdvibhurīśvaraḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*caturvidhānāṃ bhūtānāṃ pravartakanivartakaḥ \|*  
*tasyāpi bhagavān rudraḥ sākṣāddevaḥ pravartakaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*ityeṣa jyotiṣāmevaṃ saṃniveśo 'rthaniścayaḥ \|*  
*lokasaṃvyavahārārthaṃ mahādevena nirmitaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

55-58. Kṣaṇa has the nimeṣa as its first unit of time, O excellent ones among the knowers of time. Beginning with the constellation Dhaniṣṭhā and ending with Śravaṇa shall be a yuga comprising of five years. The universe whirls like a wheel due to the movement of the sun. Hence the sun is the lord and deity delimiting time. He is the instigator and castigator of the four types of living beings. Rudra, the lord himself, is the inducer of that sun. Thus the specific and fixed establishment of the luminaries and planets has been evolved by the great lord for the working of the world.

## \|\| 61.59-63 \|\|

*buddhipūrvaṃ bhagavatā kalpādau sampravartitaḥ \|*  
*sa āśrayo 'bhimānī ca sarvasya jyotirātmakaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*ekarūpapradhānasya pariṇāmo 'yamadbhutaḥ \|*  
*naiṣa śakyaḥ prasaṃkhyātuṃ yāthātathyena kenacit \|\| 60 \|\|*

*gatāgataṃ manuṣyeṇa jyotiṣāṃ māṃsacakṣuṣā \|*  
*āgamādanumānācca pratyakṣādupapattitaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

*parīkṣya nipuṇaṃ buddhyā śraddhātavyaṃ vipaścitā \|*  
*cakṣuḥ śāstraṃ jalaṃ lekhyaṃ gaṇitaṃ munisattamāḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*pañcaite hetavo jñeyā jyotirmānavinirṇaye \|\| 63 \|\|*

59-63. It has been made to function intelligently by the lord at the beginning of the kalpa. The lord is the support of all luminaries and he identifies himself with them. This is a wonderful phenomenon that is caused by the unique Pradhāna and is incomprehensible. The movement of the luminaries cannot be understood by the man with his physical eye. It can be understood by the learned man only through Vedic treatises, by inference and direct perception, by cogent arrangements and careful analysis in his mind.

## Chapter 62 - Situation of Dhruva (dhruvasaṃsthāna)

## \|\| 62.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ viṣṇoḥ prasādādvai dhruvo buddhimatāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*meḍhībhūto grāhāṇāṃ vai vaktumarhasi sāṃpratam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sages said:

1\. O foremost among the intelligent, it behoves you now to recount how, due to the grace of Viṣṇu, Dhruva became the central pivot of the planets.

## \|\| 62.2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etamarthaṃ mayā pṛṣṭo nānāśāstraviśāradaḥ \|*  
*mārkaṇḍeyaḥ purā prāha mahyaṃ śuśrūṣave dvijāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sūta said:

2\. O brahmins, when he was asked about this matter by me in former time, Mārkaṇḍeya who is an expert in different sciences said to me as I was desirous of hearing.

## \|\| 62.3 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca \|*  
*sārvabhaumo mahātejāḥ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*uttānapādo rājā vai pālayāmāsa medinīm \|\| 3 \|\|*

Mārkaṇḍeya said:

3\. An emperor of great splendour, the best among all those who wield weapons, king Uttānapāda, ruled over the earth.

## \|\| 62.4-5 \|\|

*tasya bhāryādvayam abhūt sunītiḥ surucis tathā \|*  
*agrajāyāmabhūtputraḥ sunītyāṃ tu mahāyaśāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*dhruvo nāma mahāprājñaḥ kuladīpo mahāmatiḥ \|*  
*kadācit saptavarṣe 'pi pituraṅkam upāviśat \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. He had two wives, Sunīti and Suruci. A highly intelligent son of great renown, named Dhruva was born of Sunīti the elder wife. He had great understanding and was the light of the family. When he was seven years old, once he sat in the lap of his father.

## \|\| 62.6 \|\|

*surucistaṃ vinirdhūya svaputraṃ prītimānasā \|*  
*nyaveśayattaṃ viprendrā hy aṅkaṃ rūpeṇa mānitā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O leading brahmins, Suruci who was proud of her beauty pushed him away. Delighted in her mind she placed her own son on the lap of his father.

## \|\| 62.7 \|\|

*alabdhvā sa piturdhīmān aṅkaṃ duḥkhitamānasaḥ \|*  
*mātuḥ samīpamāgamya ruroda sa punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The intelligent boy Dhruva became dejected in his mind because he was unable to occupy the lap of his father. He went to his mother and lamented.

## \|\| 62.8 \|\|

*rudantaṃ putramāhedaṃ mātā śokapariplutā \|*  
*surucirdayitā bhartus tasyāḥ putro 'pi tādṛśaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Overwhelmed by her grief the mother said to her weeping son:—“Suruci is the most beloved of her husband. Her son too is likewise.

## \|\| 62.9 \|\|

*mama tvaṃ mandabhāgyāyā jātaḥ putro 'pyabhāgyavān \|*  
*kiṃ śocasi kimarthaṃ tvaṃ rodamānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. You, a son born of me, a very unfortunate woman, are also equally unfortunate. Why do you bewail? What for do you weep again and again?

## \|\| 62.10 \|\|

*saṃtaptahṛdayo bhūtvā mama śokaṃ kariṣyasi \|*  
*svasthasthānaṃ dhruvaṃ putra svaśaktyā tvaṃ samāpnuyāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. If you are distressed in heart you will increase my sorrow. My dear son, you shall by your own power attain a more comfortable and stable abode.”

## \|\| 62.11-12 \|\|

*ityuktaḥ sa tu mātrā vai nirjagāma tadā vanam \|*  
*viśvāmitraṃ tato dṛṣṭvā praṇipatya yathāvidhi \|\| 11 \|\|*

*uvāca prāñjalirbhūtvā bhagavan vaktumarhasi \|*  
*sarveṣāmuparisthānaṃ kena prāpsyāmi sattama \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. On being advised thus by his mother he set out towards the forest. On meeting Viśvāmitra, he bowed to him duly and spoke with his palms joined in reverence:—

“O holy sir, foremost among the pious sages, it behoves you to tell me how I shall obtain a place above everyone.

## \|\| 62.13 \|\|

*pituraṅke samāsīnaṃ mātā māṃ surucirmune \|*  
*vyadhūnayatsa taṃ rājā pitā novāca kiṃcana \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O sage, I was seated on the lap of my father. My step-mother Suruci pushed me aside. My father, the king, did not protest.

## \|\| 62.14-16 \|\|

*etasmāt kāraṇād brahmaṃs trasto 'haṃ mātaraṃ gataḥ \|*  
*sunītirāha me mātā mā kṛthāḥ śokamuttamam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*svakarmaṇā paraṃ sthānaṃ prāptumarhasi putraka \|*  
*tasyā hi vacanaṃ śrutvā sthānaṃ tava mahāmune \|\| 15 \|\|*

*prāpto vanamidaṃ brahmann adya tvāṃ dṛṣṭavānprabho \|*  
*tava prasādāt prāpsye 'haṃ sthānamadbhutamuttamam \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-16. For this very reason, O brahmin, I went to my mother in fright. My mother said to me:—“O son, do not be sorry. You deserve to attain a far greater abode by your own endeavour”. On hearing her words, O great sage, I have come to you for shelter in this forest. O holy sir, O brahmin, I have now met you. By your grace I shall attain the wonderful and excellent abode.

## \|\| 62.17-18 \|\|

*ityuktaḥ sa muniḥ śrīmān prahasann idam abravīt \|*  
*rājaputra śṛṇuṣvedaṃ sthānamuttamamāpsyasi \|\| 17 \|\|*

*ārādhya jagatāmīśaṃ keśavaṃ kleśanāśanam \|*  
*dakṣiṇāṅgabhavaṃ śaṃbhor mahādevasya dhīmataḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. On being requested thus, the glorious sage said laughingly “O Prince, listen to this. You will attain an excellent abode by propitiating Keśava the lord of the worlds, and the destroyer of distress. He is born of the right limb of Śiva the intelligent great lord.

## \|\| 62.19 \|\|

*japa nityaṃ mahāprājña sarvapāpavināśanam \|*  
*iṣṭadaṃ paramaṃ śuddhaṃ pavitramamalaṃ param \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O highly intelligent one, repeat the Mantra of the lord continuously. It is great, pure and holy, it destroys all sins and yields all desires.

## \|\| 62.20 \|\|

*brūhi mantramimaṃ divyaṃ praṇavena samanvitam \|*  
*namo 'stu vāsudevāya ityevaṃ niyatendriyaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Repeat this divine Mantra controlling your sense, with the Praṇava:“namostu vāsudevāya” \[Obeisance be to Vāsudeva\]. Meditate on the eternal Viṣṇu. Be interested in japa and homa.

## \|\| 62.21-24 \|\|

*dhyāyansanātanaṃ viṣṇuṃ japahomaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*ityuktaḥ praṇipatyainaṃ viśvāmitraṃ mahāyaśāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*prāṅmukho niyato bhūtvā jajāpa prītamānasaḥ \|*  
*śākamūlaphalāhāraḥ saṃvatsaramatandritaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*jajāpa mantramaniśam ajasraṃ sa punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*vetālā rākṣasā ghorāḥ siṃhādyāś ca mahāmṛgāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*tamabhyayurmahātmānaṃ buddhimohāya bhīṣaṇāḥ \|*  
*japan sa vāsudeveti na kiṃcit pratyapadyata \|\| 24 \|\|*

21-24. On being advised thus, the boy of great renown bowed to Viśvāmitra and began his japa facing the east He restrained himself and was delighted in his mind. Alertfully he repeated the mantra continuously without break for a year, sustaining himself on vegetables, roots and fruits. Terrible vampires and demons, large fierce beasts like lions rushed at him in order to confound his wits. But, repeating the name Vāsudeva he did not take notice of anything else.

## \|\| 62.25 \|\|

*sunītir asya yā mātā tasyā rūpeṇa saṃvṛtā \|*  
*piśāci samanuprāptā ruroda bhṛśaduḥkhitā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. A female ghost assuming the form of his mother Sunīti came near him and wept bitterly and miserably.

## \|\| 62.26-27 \|\|

*mama tvamekaḥ putro 'si kimarthaṃ kliśyate bhavān \|*  
*māmanāthāmapahāya tapa āsthitavānasi \|\| 26 \|\|*

*evamādīni vākyāni bhāṣamāṇāṃ mahātapāḥ \|*  
*anirīkṣyaiva hṛṣṭātmā harernāma jajāpa saḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. “O you are my only son. Why do you torture yourself? Leaving me helpless, you have taken to penance”.

The boy continued his great penance and did not even glance at the lady who spoke thus. With delight in his heart he repeated the name Hari.

## \|\| 62.28-29 \|\|

*tataḥ praśemuḥ sarvatra vighnarūpāṇi tatra vai \|*  
*tato garuḍamāruhya kālameghasamadyutiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*sarvadevaiḥ parivṛtaḥ stūyamāno maharṣibhiḥ \|*  
*āyayau bhagavānviṣṇuḥ dhruvāntikam arātihā \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. Then all the forms of impediment and harassment subsided from all sides. Seated on Garuḍa lord Viṣṇu who resembled the black cloud in lustre, who is the destroyer of enemies, who was surrounded by Devas and who was being eulogised by great sages, came there before Dhruva.

## \|\| 62.30-31 \|\|

*samāgataṃ vilokyātha ko 'sāvityeva cintayan \|*  
*pibanniva hṛṣīkeśaṃ nayanābhyāṃ jagatpatim \|\| 30 \|\|*

*japan sa vāsudeveti dhruvastasthau mahādyutiḥ \|*  
*śaṅkhaprāntena govindaḥ pasparśāsyaṃ hi tasya vai \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. On seeing the lord come near, he simply thought within his mind “who is this?” Drinking as it were Hṛṣikeśa the lord of the Universe, by his eyes the boy of great lustre, seated himself and repeated “Vāsudeva”. With the tip of his conch the lord touched his face.

## \|\| 62.32 \|\|

*tataḥ sa paramaṃ jñānam avāpya puruṣottamam \|*  
*tuṣṭāva prāñjalirbhūtvā sarvalokeśvaraṃ harim \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Thereupon he attained the highest knowledge. With his palms joined in reverence he eulogised the lord the most excellent of all divine beings.

## \|\| 62.33 \|\|

*prasīda devadeveśa śaṅkhacakragadādhara \|*  
*lokātman vedaguhyātman tvāṃ prapanno 'smi keśava \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Be favourable, O lord of the chiefs of Devas, O wielder of conch, discus and iron club! O soul of the worlds! O soul of all, O soul of all secrets of the Vedas, O Keśava, I have sought refuge in you.

## \|\| 62.34 \|\|

*na vidustvāṃ mahātmānaṃ sanakādyā maharṣayaḥ \|*  
*tatkathaṃ tvāmahaṃ vidyāṃ namaste bhuvaneśvara \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Even the great sages Sanaka and others have not comprehended you, the great Ātman. Then how can I know you? O lord of the worlds, obeisance to you.

## \|\| 62.35 \|\|

*tamāha prahasanviṣṇur ehi vatsa dhruvo bhavān \|*  
*sthānaṃ dhruvaṃ samāsādya jyotiṣām agrabhug bhava \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Then Viṣṇu said to him smiling:—“O dear one, come on. You are Dhruva (steady). Attaining a fixed and steady abode be the first among all luminaries.

## \|\| 62.36 \|\|

*mātrā tvaṃ sahitastatra jyotiṣāṃ sthānamāpnuhi \|*  
*matsthānametatparamaṃ dhruvaṃ nityaṃ suśobhanam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. You along with your mother shall attain the abode of luminaries. This abode is mine, the greatest, the steady splendid abode.

## \|\| 62.37-38 \|\|

*tapasārādhya deveśaṃ purā labdhaṃ hi śaṅkarāt \|*  
*vāsudeveti yo nityaṃ praṇavena samanvitam \|\| 37 \|\|*

*namaskārasamāyuktaṃ bhagavacchabdasaṃyutam \|*  
*japedevaṃ hi yo vidvān dhruvaṃ sthānaṃ prapadyate \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. It was acquired by me from lord Śiva formerly after propitiating him by penance. The devotee who repeats continuously the name Vāsudeva along with the Praṇava ‘om’ the word ‘Bhagavat’ and the word ‘namas’ denoting obeisance attains the fixed abode of Dhruva.”

## \|\| 62.39-42 \|\|

*tato devāḥ sagandharvāḥ siddhāś ca paramarṣayaḥ \|*  
*mātrā saha dhruvaṃ sarve tasmin sthāne nyaveśayan \|\| 39 \|\|*

*viṣṇorājñāṃ puraskṛtya jyotiṣāṃ sthānamāptavān \|*  
*evaṃ dhruvo mahātejā dvādaśākṣaravidyayā \|\| 40 \|\|*

*avāpa mahatīṃ siddhim etatte kathitaṃ mayā \|\| 41 \|\|*

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasmādyo vāsudevāya praṇāmaṃ kurute naraḥ \|*  
*sa yāti dhruvasālokyaṃ dhruvatvaṃ tasya tattathā \|\| 42 \|\|*

39-42. Then all Devas, Siddhas, sages and Gandharvas installed Dhruva in that abode along with his mother. Thus, at the behest of Viṣṇu he attained the abode of luminaries. By means of the twelve-syllabled mantra, Dhruva of great splendour attained the highest perfection.

Sūta said:

## Chapter 63 - Origin of Devas and others (devādi-sṛṣṭi)

## \|\| 63.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*devānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca gandharvoragarakṣasām \|*  
*utpattiṃ brūhi sūtādya yathākramamanuttamam \|\| 1 \|\|*

The sages said:

1\. O Sūta, recount the origin of Devas, Dānavas, Gandharvas, Serpents and Rākṣasas, in an excellent way and in due order.

## \|\| 63.2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*saṃkalpāddarśanātsparśāt pūrveṣāṃ sṛṣṭirucyate \|*  
*dakṣātprācetasādūrdhvaṃ sṛṣṭirmaithunasaṃbhavā \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sūta said:

2\. The creation of ancient people was by means of mental conception, direct perception or touch. Subsequent to Dakṣa the son of Pracetas, creation is by means of sexual intercourse.

## \|\| 63.3-6 \|\|

*yadā tu sṛjatastasya devarṣigaṇapannagān \|*  
*na vṛddhimagamallokas tadā maithunayogataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*dakṣaḥ putrasahasrāṇi pañca sūtyāmajījanat \|*  
*tāṃstu dṛṣṭvā mahābhāgān sisṛkṣurvividhāḥ prajāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*nāradaḥ prāha haryaśvān dakṣaputrān samāgatān \|*  
*bhuvaḥ pramāṇaṃ sarvaṃ tu jñātvordhvamadha eva ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tataḥ sṛṣṭiṃ viśeṣeṇa kurudhvaṃ munisattamāḥ \|*  
*te tu tadvacanaṃ śrutvā prayātāḥ sarvatodiśam \|\| 6 \|\|*

3-6. When he began to create the group of Devas, sages and serpents, the world did not increase. Thereupon, by means of sexual intercourse, Dakṣa begot of Sūti, five thousand sons.

On seeing those blessed ones who were desirous of creating different kinds of progeny, Nārada spoke to Haryaśvas, the sons of Dakṣa who had assembled together.

“Understand the extent of the earth from above and below, O excellent sages, and then proceed ahead with your special creation.”

On hearing his words they went away in all directions.

## \|\| 63.7-10 \|\|

*adyāpi na nivartante samudrādiva sindhavaḥ \|*  
*haryaśveṣu ca naṣṭeṣu punardakṣaḥ prajāpatiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*sūtyāmeva ca putrāṇāṃ sahasramasṛjatprabhuḥ \|*  
*śabalā nāma te viprāḥ sametāḥ sṛṣṭihetavaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*nārado 'nugatānprāha punastānsūryavarcasaḥ \|*  
*bhuvaḥ pramāṇaṃ sarvaṃ tu jñātvā bhrātṝn punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*āgatya vātha sṛṣṭiṃ vai kariṣyatha viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*te 'pi tenaiva mārgeṇa jagmurbhrātṛgatiṃ tathā \|\| 10 \|\|*

7-10. Even today they have not returned like the rivers after joining the ocean.

When Haryaśvas vanished, lord Dakṣa Prajāpati begot of Sūti herself another thousand sons. O brahmins, they were named Śabalas and they assembled together for the purpose of creation.

Nārada spoke to those persons of solar splendour, who had assembled before him—“You should proceed with your special creation after understanding the full extent of the earth, or on return after finding out what has happened to your brothers.

They too followed their brothers and attained the same goal as their brothers before.

## \|\| 63.11 \|\|

*tatasteṣvapi naṣṭeṣu ṣaṣṭikanyāḥ prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*vairiṇyāṃ janayāmāsa dakṣaḥ prācetasastadā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. When they too vanished the Prajāpati Dakṣa the son of Pracetas, begot sixty daughters of Vīriṇī.

## \|\| 63.12-15 \|\|

*prādātsa daśakaṃ dharme kaśyapāya trayodaśa \|*  
*viṃśatsapta ca somāya catasro 'riṣṭanemaye \|\| 12 \|\|*

*dve caiva bhṛguputrāya dve kṛśāśvāya dhīmate \|*  
*dve caivāṅgirase tadvat tāsāṃ nāmāni vistarāt \|\| 13 \|\|*

*śṛṇudhvaṃ devamātṝṇāṃ prajāvistāramāditaḥ \|*  
*marutvatī vasūr yāmir lambā bhānurarundhatī \|\| 14 \|\|*

*saṃkalpā ca muhūrtā ca sādhyā viśvā ca bhāminī*  
*dharmapatnyaḥ samākhyātās tāsāṃ putrānvadāmi vaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

12- 15. He gave ten of them in marriage to Dharma, thirteen to Kaśyapa, twentyseven to the moon, four to Ariṣṭanemi, two to the son of Bhṛgu, two to the intelligent Kṛśāśva and two to Aṅgiras. Now listen to the names of the mothers of Devas and the details of their progeny from the very beginning.

The ten wives of Dharma were:—Marutvatī, Vasū, Yāmi, Lambā, Bhanu, Arundhatī, Saṅkalpā, Muhūrtā, Sādhyā and Viśvā.

I shall tell you the names of their sons.

## \|\| 63.16-26 \|\|

*viśvedevāstu viśvāyāḥ sādhyā sādhyānajījanat \|*  
*marutvatyāṃ marutvanto vasostu vasavas tathā \|\| 16 \|\|*

*bhānostu bhānavaḥ proktā muhūrtāyā muhūrtakāḥ \|*  
*lambāyā ghoṣanāmāno nāgavīthistu yāmijaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*saṃkalpāyāstu saṃkalpo vasusargaṃ vadāmi vaḥ \|*  
*jyotiṣmantastu ye devā vyāpakāḥ sarvatodiśam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*vasavaste samākhyātāḥ sarvabhūtahitaiṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*āpo dhruvaś ca somaś ca dharaścaivānilo 'nalaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*pratyūṣaś ca prabhāsaś ca vasavo 'ṣṭau prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*ajaikapād ahirbudhnyo virūpākṣaḥ sabhairavaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*haraś ca bahurūpaś ca tryaṃbakaś ca sureśvaraḥ \|*  
*sāvitraś ca jayantaś ca pinākī cāparājitaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*ete rudrāḥ samākhyātā ekādaśa gaṇeśvarāḥ \|*  
*kaśyapasya pravakṣyāmi patnībhyaḥ putrapautrakam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*aditiś ca ditiścaiva ariṣṭā surasā muniḥ \|*  
*surabhir vinatā tāmrā tadvat krodhavaśā ilā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*kadrūstviṣā danustadvat tāsāṃ putrānvadāmi vaḥ \|*  
*tuṣitā nāma ye devāś cākṣuṣasyāntare manoḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*vaivasvatāntare te vai ādityā dvādaśa smṛtāḥ \|*  
*indro dhātā bhagastvaṣṭa mitro 'tha varuṇo 'ryamā \|\| 25 \|\|*

*vivasvānsavitā pūṣā aṃśumān viṣṇureva ca \|*  
*ete sahasrakiraṇā ādityā dvādaśa smṛtāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

16-20a. The Viśvedevas were born to Viśvā. Sādhyā bore the Sādhyas. Marutvats were born of Marutvatī. Vasus were born of Vasū. The Bhānus were born of Bhānu; the Muhūrtakas were born of Muhūrta; the Ghoṣas were born of Lambā. Nāgavīthī was born of Yāmi. Saṅkalpa was born of Saṅkalpā. I shall tell you the creation of the Vasus. Devas who are luminous and who pervade all the quarters are called Vasus. They are the well wishers of all living beings. They are reputed to be eight, viz.—Āpa, Dhruva, Soma, Dharā, Anila, Anala, Pratyūṣa and Prabhāsa.

20b-22a. The eleven Rudras, the leaders of the Gaṇas are:—Ajaikapād, Ahirbudhnya, Virūpākṣa, Bhairava, Hara, Bahurūpa, Tryambaka the lord of Devas, Sāvitra, Jayanta, Pinākin and Aparājita.

22b-26. I shall mention the sons and grandsons of Kaśyapa from his thirteen wives:—Aditi, Diti Ariṣṭā, Surasā, Muni, Surabhi, Vinatā, Tāmrā, Krodhavaśā, Ilā, Kadrū, Tviṣā and Danu.

I shall tell you the names of the sons of these.

Devas who were known as Tuṣitas in the Cākṣuṣa manvantara are spoken of as the twelve Ādityas in the Vaivasvata manvantara. The following twelve are the thousand-rayed Ādityas:—

Indra, Dhātṛ, Bhaga, Tvaṣṭṛ, Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman, Vivasvān, Savitṛ, Pūṣan, Aṃśumat and Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 63.27 \|\|

*ditiḥ putradvayaṃ lebhe kaśyapāditi naḥ śrutam \|*  
*hiraṇyakaśipuṃ caiva hiraṇyākṣaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. We have heard that Diti had two sons from Kaśyapa viz, Hiraṇyakaśipu and Hiraṇyākṣa

## \|\| 63.28 \|\|

*danuḥ putraśataṃ lebhe kaśyapād baladarpitam \|*  
*vipracittiḥ pradhāno 'bhūt teṣāṃ madhye dvijottamāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Danu bore a hundred sons to Kaśyapa. They were mighty and arrogant. O excellent brahmins, among them Vipracitti was the chief.

## \|\| 63.29 \|\|

*tāmrā ca janayāmāsa ṣaṭ kanyā dvijapuṅgavāḥ \|*  
*śukīṃ śyenīṃ ca bhāsīṃ ca sugrīvīṃ gṛdhrikāṃ śucim \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O leading brahmins, Tāmrā bore six daughters viz.—Śukī, Śyenī, Bhāsī, Sugrīvī, Gṛdhrikā and Śuci.

## \|\| 63.30-31 \|\|

*śukī śukānulūkāṃś ca janayāmāsa dharmataḥ \|*  
*śyenī śyenāṃs tathā bhāsī kuraṅgāṃś ca vyajījanat \|\| 30 \|\|*

*gṛdhrī gṛdhrān kapotāṃś ca pārāvatī vihaṃgamān \|*  
*haṃsasārasakāraṇḍaplavāñchucirajījanat \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. Śukī duly gave birth to parrots and owls. Śyenī gave birth to hawks (falcons), etc. Bhāsī gave birth to deers. Gṛdhrī bore the vultures, doves, pigeons and other birds. Śuci gave birth to swans, cranes and other aquatic birds such as Kāraṇḍa, Plava.

## \|\| 63.32-34 \|\|

*ajāśvameṣoṣṭrakharān sugrīvī cāpyajījanat \|*  
*vinatā janayāmāsa garuḍaṃ cāruṇaṃ śubhā \|\| 32 \|\|*

*saudāminīṃ tathā kanyāṃ sarvalokabhayaṅkarīm \|*  
*surasāyāḥ sahasraṃ tu sarpāṇāmabhavatpurā \|\| 33 \|\|*

*kadrūḥ sahasraśirasāṃ sahasraṃ prāpa suvratā \|*  
*pradhānāsteṣu vikhyātāḥ ṣaḍviṃśatiranuttamāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

32-34. Sugrīvī gave birth to goats, horses, sheep, camels and donkeys. Vinatā gave birth to Garuḍa and Aruṇa, (two sons) and then a daughter Saudāminī (lightning) terrible unto all the worlds.

A thousand cobras were born to Surasā. Kadru gave birth to a thousand thousand-hooded serpents. Twenty-six excellent ones among them are well known as their chiefs.

## \|\| 63.35-37 \|\|

*śeṣavāsukikarkoṭaśaṅkhairāvatakambalāḥ \|*  
*dhanañjayamahānīlapadmāśvataratakṣakāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*elāpatramahāpadmadhṛtarāṣṭrabalāhakāḥ \|*  
*śaṅkhapālamahāśaṅkhapuṣpadaṃṣṭraśubhānanāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*śaṅkhalomā ca nahuṣo vāmanaḥ phaṇitas tathā \|*  
*kapilo durmukhaścāpi patañjaliriti smṛtaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

35-37. They are:—Śeṣa, Vāsuki, Karkoṭa, Śaṅkha, Airāvata, Kambala, Dhanañjaya, Mahānīla, Padma, Aśvatara, Takṣaka, Elāpatra, Mahāpadma, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Balāhaka, Śaṅkhapāla, Mahāśaṅkha, Puṣpadaṃṣṭra, Śubhānana, Śaṅkhaloman, Nahuṣa, Vāmana, Phaṇita, Kapila, Durmukha and Patañjali.

## \|\| 63.38-41 \|\|

*rakṣogaṇaṃ krodhavaśā mahāmāyaṃ vyajījanat \|*  
*rudrāṇāṃ ca gaṇaṃ tadvad gomahiṣyau varāṅganā \|\| 38 \|\|*

*surabhir janayāmāsa kaśyapāditi naḥ śrutam \|*  
*munirmunīnāṃ ca gaṇaṃ gaṇamapsarasāṃ tathā \|\| 39 \|\|*

*tathā kiṃnaragandharvān ariṣṭājanayadbahūn \|*  
*tṛṇavṛkṣalatāgulmam ilā sarvamajījanat \|\| 40 \|\|*

*tviṣā tu yakṣarakṣāṃsi janayāmāsa koṭiśaḥ \|*  
*ete tu kāśyapeyāś ca saṃkṣepātparikīrtitāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

38-41. Krodhavaśā gave birth to the Rākṣasas wielding great power of deception and also the group of Rudras. The excellent lady Surabhi, gave birth to cows and buffaloes as the children of Kaśyapa. Muni gave birth to the group of sages and Apsaras. Ariṣṭā gave birth to Kinnaras and Gandharvas. Ilā gave birth to grasses, trees, creepers and hedges. Tviṣā gave birth to crores and crores of Yakṣas and Rākṣasas

These are the immediate descendants of Kaśyapa, narrated succinctly.

## \|\| 63.42-45 \|\|

*eteṣāṃ putrapautrādivaṃśāś ca bahavaḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*evaṃ prajāsu sṛṣṭāsu kaśyapena mahātmanā \|\| 42 \|\|*

*pratiṣṭhitāsu sarvāsu carāsu sthāvarāsu ca \|*  
*abhiṣicyādhipatyeṣu teṣāṃ mukhyānprajāpatiḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*tato manuṣyādhipatiṃ cakre vaivasvataṃ manum \|*  
*svāyaṃbhuve 'ntare pūrvaṃ brahmaṇā ye 'bhiṣecitāḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*tairiyaṃ pṛthivī sarvā saptadvīpā saparvatā \|*  
*yathopadeśamadyāpi dharmeṇa pratipālyate \|\| 45 \|\|*

42-45. These had their own numerous sons, grandsons etc. Their races are many. After the children had been procreated by the noble Kaśyapa, after all the mobile and immobile beings had been well established, Prajapati crowned the chief ones among each of them as overlords. He made Vaivasvata Manu the overlord of human beings. Those who were crowned by Brahmā in the Svāyambhuva manvantara, even now protect and rule over the earth with its seven continents and mountains. They rule virtuously in accordance with the instructions of the lord.

## \|\| 63.46 \|\|

*svāyaṃbhuve 'ntare pūrve brahmaṇā ye 'bhiṣecitāḥ \|*  
*te hyete cābhiṣicyante manavaś ca bhavanti te \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Only those who had been crowned formerly in the Svāyambhuva manvantara by Brahmā are crowned now. They become the Manus.

## \|\| 63.47-49 \|\|

*manvantareṣvatīteṣu gatā hyeteṣu pārthivāḥ \|*  
*evamanye 'bhiṣicyante prāpte manvantare tataḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*atītānāgatāḥ sarve nṛpā manvantare smṛtāḥ \|*  
*etānutpādya putrāṃstu prajāsaṃtānakāraṇāt \|\| 48 \|\|*

*kaśyapo gotrakāmastu cacāra sa punastapaḥ \|*  
*putro gotrakaro mahyaṃ bhavatād iti cintayan \|\| 49 \|\|*

47-49. In the past manvantaras these had been the kings. Others are being crowned when a new manvantara arrives. All the kings of the past and future manvantaras are mentioned in detail.

After procreating these sons for the continuity of the race Kaśyapa performed penance once again with the desire to have a son who will preserve the spiritual line.

## \|\| 63.50-51 \|\|

*tasyaivaṃ dhyāyamānasya kaśyapasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*brahmayogātsutau paścāt prādurbhūtau mahaujasau \|\| 50 \|\|*

*vatsaraścāsitaścaiva tāvubhau brahmavādinau \|*  
*vatsarānnaidhruvo jajñe raibhyaś ca sumahāyaśāḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. Even as Kaśyapa was meditating thus, two sons of great prowess manifested themselves by the grace of Brahman. Those two Vatsara and Asita were expounders of Brahman. Naidhruva and Raibhya were born of Vatsara.

## \|\| 63.52-54 \|\|

*raibhyasya raibhyā vijñeyā naidhruvasya vadāmi vaḥ \|*  
*cyavanasya tu kanyāyāṃ sumedhāḥ samapadyata \|\| 52 \|\|*

*naidhruvasya tu sā patnī mātā vai kuṇḍapāyinām \|*  
*asitasyaikaparṇāyāṃ brahmiṣṭhaḥ samapadyata \|\| 53 \|\|*

*śāṇḍilyānāṃ varaḥ śrīmān devalaḥ sumahātapāḥ \|*  
*śāṇḍilyā naidhruvā raibhyās trayaḥ pakṣāstu kāśyapāḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

52-54. The sons of Raibhya are known as Raibhyas. I shall mention those of Naidhruva. Sumedhas was born of the daughter of Cyavana. She became the wife of Naidhruva and the mother of Kuṇḍapāyins.

The glorious son Devala was born of Ekaparṇā and Asita. He was a knower of Brāhman, the best of all the Śāṇḍilyas and one possessing great penance. Thus the descendants of Kaśyapa became three branches; Śāṇḍilyas, Naidhruvas and Raibhyas.

## \|\| 63.55-58 \|\|

*nava prakṛtayo devāḥ pulastyasya vadāmi vaḥ \|*  
*caturyuge hyatikrānte manorekādaśe prabhoḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*ardhāvaśiṣṭe tasmiṃstu dvāpare sampravartite \|*  
*mānavasya nariṣyantaḥ putra āsīd damaḥ kila \|\| 56 \|\|*

*damasya tasya dāyādas tṛṇabinduriti smṛtaḥ \|*  
*tretāyugamukhe rājā tṛtīye saṃbabhūva ha \|\| 57 \|\|*

*tasya kanyā tvilavilā rūpeṇāpratimābhavat \|*  
*pulastyāya sa rājarṣis tāṃ kanyāṃ pratyapādayat \|\| 58 \|\|*

55-58. Devas had nine sources of origin. I shall mention the line of Pulastya.

After eleven cycles of four yugas have practically passed by when Manu was the lord and half the period of Dvāpara had passed by, Dama was born as the son of Nariṣyanta, a descendant of Manu. Dama’s descendant known as Tṛṇabindu became king in the third quarter of Tretāyuga. His daughter Ilavilā was unrivalled in beauty and the king gave her in marriage to Pulastya.

## \|\| 63.59 \|\|

*ṛṣir airavilo yasyāṃ viśravāḥ samapadyata \|*  
*tasya patnyaścatasrastu paulastyakulavardhanāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Viśravas the great sage was born of Ilavilā. His four wives are the progenitors of the famity of Pulastya.

## \|\| 63.60-65 \|\|

*bṛhaspateḥ śubhā kanyā nāmnā vai devavarṇinī*  
*puṣpotkaṭā balākā ca sute mālyavataḥ smṛteḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

*kaikasī mālinaḥ kanyā tāsāṃ vai śṛṇuta prajāḥ \|*  
*jyeṣṭhaṃ vaiśravaṇaṃ tasmāt suṣuve devavarṇinī \|\| 61 \|\|*

*kaikasī cāpyajanayad rāvaṇaṃ rākṣasādhipam \|*  
*kumbhakarṇaṃ śūrpaṇakhāṃ dhīmantaṃ ca vibhīṣaṇam \|\| 62 \|\|*

*puṣpotkaṭā hyajanayat putrāṃstasmāddvijottamāḥ \|*  
*mahodaraṃ prahastaṃ ca mahāpārśvaṃ kharaṃ tathā \|\| 63 \|\|*

*kumbhīnasīṃ tathā kanyāṃ balāyāḥ śṛṇuta prajāḥ \|*  
*triśirā dūṣaṇaścaiva vidyujjihvaś ca rākṣasaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

*kanyā vai mālikā cāpi balāyāḥ prasavaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*ityete krūrakarmāṇaḥ paulastyā rākṣasā nava \|\| 65 \|\|*

60-65. The first wife Devavarṇinī was the splendid daughter of Bṛhaspati. The second and third wives were the two daughters of Mālyavān, viz. Puṣpotkaṭā and Balākā and the fourth wife Kaikasī was the daughter of Mālin.

Now listen to the children of these ladies. Devavarṇinī bore the eldest son Vaiśravaṇa to him. Kaikasī gave birth to Rāvaṇa, the king of Rākṣasas, Kumbhakarṇa, Śūrpaṇakhā and Vibhīṣaṇa. O excellent brahmins, Puṣpotkaṭā bore him Mahodara, Prahasta, Mahāpārśva, Khara and the daughter Kumbhīnasī. Now listen to the childern of Balā \[i. e. Balākā\]. They were Triśiras, Dūṣana, Vidyujjihva and the daughter Mālikā. Thus the Rākṣasas of ruthless activities belonging to the family of Pulastya are nine.

## \|\| 63.66-68 \|\|

*vibhīṣaṇo 'tiśuddhātmā dharmajñaḥ parikīrtitaḥ \|*  
*pulastyasya mṛgāḥ putrāḥ sarve vyāghrāś ca daṃṣṭriṇaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*bhūtāḥ piśācāḥ sarpāś ca sūkarā hastinas tathā \|*  
*vānarāḥ kiṃnarāścaiva ye ca kiṃpuruṣās tathā \|\| 67 \|\|*

*anapatyaḥ kratustasmin smṛto vaivasvate 'ntare \|*  
*atreḥ patnyo daśaivāsan suṃdaryaś ca pativratāḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

66-68. Vibhīṣaṇa is glorified as the knower of Dharma. He was a highly pure soul.

The deer, the fanged animals, tigers, goblins, ghosts, serpents, boars, elephants, monkeys, Kinnaras and Kimpuruṣas were the sons of Pulastya.

In the Vaivasvata manvantara Kratu is said to be issueless, Atri had ten beautiful and chaste wives.

## \|\| 63.69-70 \|\|

*bhadrāśvasya ghṛtācyāṃ vai daśāpsarasi sūnavaḥ \|*  
*bhadrābhadrā ca jaladā mandā nandā tathaiva ca \|\| 69 \|\|*

*balābalā ca viprendrā yā ca gopābalā smṛtā \|*  
*tathā tāmarasā caiva varakrīḍā ca vai daśa \|\| 70 \|\|*

69-70. Bhadrāśva begot of the celestial damsel Ghṛtāci ten children viz Bhadrā, Abhadrā, Jaladā, Mandā, Ānandā (or Nandā), Balā, Abalā, Gopābalā, Tāmarasā and Varakrīḍā

## \|\| 63.71-73 \|\|

*ātreyavaṃśaprabhavās tāsāṃ bhartā prabhākaraḥ \|*  
*svarbhānupihite sūrye patite 'smindivo mahīm \|\| 71 \|\|*

*tamo 'bhibhūte loke 'smin prabhā yena pravartitā \|*  
*svastyastu hi tavetyukte patanniha divākaraḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

*brahmarṣervacanāttasya papāta na vibhurdivaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ prabhākaretyuktaḥ prabhuratrirmaharṣibhiḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

71-73. These are the progenitors of the family of Ātreya. Their husband is Prabhākara. When the sun was swallowed by Rāhu and he fell down towards the earth from the heavens the whole world was enveloped in darkness. At that time Atri spread lustre everywhere. He said “Hail to Thee” and then the falling sun ceased to fall at the instance of the brahmin sage. Then Atri was called Prabhākara by the great sages.

## \|\| 63.74 \|\|

*bhadrāyāṃ janayāmāsa somaṃ putraṃ yaśasvinam \|*  
*sa tāsu janayāmāsa punaḥ putrāṃstapodhanaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. He begot of Bhadrā the renowned son Soma (Moon). The sage procreated more sons of those wives.

## \|\| 63.75 \|\|

*svastyātreyā iti khyātā ṛṣayo vedapāragāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ dvau khyātayaśasau brahmiṣṭhau ca mahaujasau \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. They are well known as Svastyātreyas. They were sages and masters of the Vedas. Two of them became well renowned. They had realised Brahman. They were very powerful.

## \|\| 63.76 \|\|

*datto hyatrivaro jyeṣṭho durvāsāstasya cānujaḥ \|*  
*yavīyasī svasā teṣām amalā brahmavādinī \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Datta was the eldest son of Atri. Durvāsas was his younger brother. The youngest sister was Amalā, an expounder of the Brahman.

## \|\| 63.77 \|\|

*tasya gotradvaye jātāś catvāraḥ prathitā bhuvi \|*  
*śyāvaś ca pratvasaścaiva vavalguścātha gahvaraḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Four of them born of two Gotras are well known in the world, viz. Śyāva, Pratvasa, Vavalgu and Gahvara.

## \|\| 63.78 \|\|

*ātreyāṇāṃ ca catvāraḥ smṛtāḥ pakṣā mahātmanām \|*  
*kāśyapo nāradaścaiva parvatānuddhatas tathā \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Four lines of the spiritual family of Ātreyas of noble souls are known as Kāśyapa, Nārada, Parvata and Anuddhata.

## \|\| 63.79 \|\|

*jajñire mānasā hyete arundhatyā nibodhata \|*  
*nāradastu vasiṣṭhāyā-rundhatīṃ pratyapādayat \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. These were born as mental sons. Now understand the children of Arundhatī. It was Nārada who gave Arundhatī to Vasiṣṭha.

## \|\| 63.80-82 \|\|

*ūrdhvaretā mahātejā dakṣaśāpāttu nāradaḥ \|*
